STANDARD LIBRARY
Reference / io/stdout

io/stdout#

The process's standard output and standard error.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

Stdout().writeln("ready");
Stdout().write("answer: ", answer.string());
Stdout() <- "raw UTF-8 text" <- packet <- "\n";
Stderr().writeln("cannot continue");

Description#

The process's standard output and standard error.

Stdout().writeln("ready");
ready

Both are Writing (bytes) and WritingText (text). Text is written as strict UTF-8, arguments in order with no separators; writeln adds one LF after them. Nothing formats values on its own: write .string() or use strings/format. Byte writes keep the exact octets of a ByteSource or an @byte.

Standard output is buffered by the runtime, for every Stdout value at once: a terminal gets each line as it ends, a pipe or a file gets the bytes in blocks. Stdout().flush() writes out what is pending; the runtime also does that before anything goes to standard error, before standard input is read from a terminal, before a child process starts and when the program ends. Standard error is not buffered.

Public API#

object Stdout#

object Stdout does Writing, WritingText

Standard output. Every Stdout value writes to the same buffered stream.

Stdout.Stdout#

Stdout()

The process's standard output.

Stdout.write#

write(source is ByteSource) is void

Writes the bytes of a ByteSource exactly, for example Utf8Encoded(text).

Stdout.write#

write(bytes is @byte) is void

Writes the bytes as they are.

Stdout.flush#

flush() is void

Writes out what the buffer holds.

Stdout.write#

write(values is ...string) is void

Writes the strings as UTF-8, one after another, with nothing between them.

Stdout.writeln#

writeln(values is ...string) is void

Writes the strings as UTF-8 and then one LF: Stdout().writeln("total: ", total.string()).

object Stderr#

object Stderr does Writing, WritingText

Standard error. It is not buffered; whatever Stdout holds goes out first, so the two keep their order.

Stderr.Stderr#

Stderr()

The process's standard error.

Stderr.write#

write(source is ByteSource) is void

Writes the bytes of a ByteSource exactly.

Stderr.write#

write(bytes is @byte) is void

Writes the bytes as they are.

Stderr.flush#

flush() is void

Nothing to do: standard error is not buffered.

Stderr.write#

write(values is ...string) is void

Writes the strings as UTF-8, one after another, with nothing between them.

Stderr.writeln#

writeln(values is ...string) is void

Writes the strings as UTF-8 and then one LF.

Errors#

A write the system takes only in part throws IncompleteWrite.after(written) with the bytes taken; nothing is retried.
